directAnswer: To force quit an app on a Mac, you can use the 'Force Quit Applications' window or the keyboard shortcut Command + Option + Esc.
summary: This guide provides steps to force quit unresponsive applications on macOS, along with common questions and important considerations.

sections.heading: Using the Force Quit Applications Window
sections.body: You can access the Force Quit Applications window to see all currently running applications and force quit any that are unresponsive.

sections.heading: Using Keyboard Shortcut
sections.body: The keyboard shortcut Command + Option + Esc opens the Force Quit Applications window directly, allowing you to quickly select and quit an app.

steps.title: Open the Force Quit Applications Window
steps.detail: Press Command + Option + Esc to open the Force Quit Applications window.

steps.title: Select the Unresponsive App
steps.detail: In the list, click on the application that is not responding.

steps.title: Force Quit the App
steps.detail: Click the 'Force Quit' button to close the selected application.

steps.title: Using Activity Monitor (Alternative Method)
steps.detail: Open 'Activity Monitor' from Applications > Utilities, select the app, and click the 'X' button to force quit.

faqs.question: What should I do if the app doesn't close after force quitting?
faqs.answer: If the app still doesn't close, try restarting your Mac or using Activity Monitor to terminate the process.

faqs.question: Will I lose unsaved work if I force quit an app?
faqs.answer: Yes, force quitting an app may result in loss of unsaved changes, so it's best to save your work regularly.

faqs.question: Can I force quit system applications?
faqs.answer: While you can force quit system applications, it may cause instability in your system, so proceed with caution.

caveats: Force quitting may lead to data loss for unsaved work in the application.
